what_its_for: Ixekizumab is used to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis (a skin condition that causes red, scaly patches), psoriatic arthritis (joint pain and swelling linked to psoriasis), ankylosing spondylitis (a type of spine arthritis), and non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (back and joint inflammation that does not yet show up on X-rays). It works by blocking a protein in your body called IL-17A that causes inflammation.
how_to_take: Ixekizumab comes as a liquid in a pre-filled autoinjector pen or pre-filled syringe that you inject under the skin (subcutaneous injection). Your doctor or nurse will show you how to inject it the first time. You can inject it into your stomach (abdomen), thigh, or upper outer arm. Rotate injection sites each time and do not inject into skin that is sore, bruised, red, hard, or affected by psoriasis. Remove the pen or syringe from the refrigerator and let it sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before injecting. Do not shake the device.
dosing: For plaque psoriasis in adults: The starting dose is 160 mg (two 80 mg injections) at Week 0, then 80 mg every 2 weeks for the first 12 weeks, then 80 mg once a month (every 4 weeks) after that. For psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis: The usual dose is 160 mg at Week 0, then 80 mg every 4 weeks. Dosing for children may be different and is based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then go back to your regular dosing schedule. Do not inject two doses at the same time or within a few days of each other to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store ixekizumab in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it and do not use it if it has been frozen. Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 5 days, but do not put it back in the refrigerator after that. Throw it away if it has been at room temperature for more than 5 days. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used pens and syringes in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive live vaccines (such as MMR, chickenpox, or nasal flu vaccine) while using ixekizumab, as this may cause serious infections. Avoid being around people who are sick, especially with infections like colds, flu, or chickenpox. Avoid activities that increase your risk of cuts or wounds that could get infected. Tell your doctor about all other medications, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some medicines may interact with ixekizumab.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you have: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, sweats, cough, shortness of breath, burning when you urinate, or a wound that will not heal; signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, rash, or hives; new or worsening stomach pain or diarrhea (which could be signs of inflammatory bowel disease); chest tightness or pain; or any new or unusual symptoms. Also tell your doctor if you have a history of tuberculosis (TB), Crohn's disease, or ulcerative colitis before starting this medication.
when_it_works: Some people begin to notice improvement in their skin or joint symptoms within 1 to 2 weeks of starting treatment. Most people see significant improvement by 12 weeks. It may take a few months to see the full benefit of the medication. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not notice immediate results.
special_populations: Pregnancy: It is not known if ixekizumab is safe during pregnancy. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or become pregnant while using this medication. Breastfeeding: It is not known if ixekizumab passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Ixekizumab is approved for children 6 years and older with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis. The dose is based on the child's body weight. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustment is needed for older adults, but they may be at higher risk for infections. Patients with active infections or tuberculosis should not start ixekizumab until the infection is treated and resolved.
